newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ROWELL RECALLS GRAYSON AND GIVES FIRST CAP TO HILL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ROWELL RECALLS GRAYSON AND GIVES FIRST CAP TO HILL.

text.p: Coach Jack Rowell finally addressed the two glaring deficiencies in the England rugby side on Monday when he replaced Mike Catt at fly-half and selected a specialist open-side flanker for the Five Nations' international against Scotland on February 1.
Catt, a talented footballer, looked woefully out of place at stand-off during England's pre-Christmas internationals and his goal kicking was also inconsistent.
He is replaced by Paul Grayson who looked competent and composed in last year's championship while Saracens' flanker Richard Hill wins a first cap on the side of the scrum.
Lawrence Dallaglio, who never looked at home on the open side, reverts to blind-side flanker with Tim Rodber shifting to number eight in place of Chris Sheasby.
''I am a bit surprised but obviously delighted to have this chance to prove myself at the highest level,'' Hill said.
Rowell said England had selected Catt in the belief they needed an attacking number eight.

''Mike Catt was running hot but the question was 'could he do it at international level'?,'' Rowell said. ''Regretfully, while he showed flashes of brilliance, we needed someone to run a game and Mike's kicking came increasingly under pressure.
''So we've reverted to last year's Five Nations' number 10. What gives Paul Grayson the edge not least is his place-kicking.''
Rowell has also kept faith with former captain Will Carling at centre instead of Jeremy Guscott to partner skipper Phil de Glanville.
''In terms of Carling and Guscott, we went with Will Carling who is a pace-power individual,'' Rowell added.
''Jerry Guscott is at the other end of the spectrum and I say that constructively. But the way the game's going, Carling is a very robust individual.''

England - Tim Stimpson; Jon Sleightholme, Will Carling, Phil de Glanville (captain), Tony Underwood; Paul Grayson, Andy Gomarsall; Tim Rodber, Richard Hill, Lawrence Dallaglio, Simon Shaw, Martin Johnson, Jason Leonard, Mark Regan, Graham Rowntree.
